extracted.intended_audience: institutional investors, delegated-voting clients, corporate governance and stewardship professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Annual corporate investment stewardship report describing BIS (BlackRock Investment Stewardship) policies, processes, governance, engagement priorities, voting practices, vendor oversight, conflict management, and reporting to clients. Provides standards and operational expectations for stewardship activity executed on behalf of index equity clients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term investor perspective / financial materiality-based approach
rubrics_metrics.description: BIS’ stewardship program is conducted from the perspective of a long-term investor and takes a financial materiality-based approach, focused solely on advancing clients’ investment objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stewardship, including engagement and voting on behalf of clients, assesses how companies are creating long-term financial value; activities are directed at protecting and enhancing clients’ long-term financial interests (e.g., investors saving for retirement).

rubrics_metrics.name: BIS Benchmark Policies (Global Principles, Regional voting guidelines, Engagement Priorities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain global principles on corporate governance (Global Principles) that guide stewardship while recognizing unique characteristics of different markets, supported by regional voting guidelines and Engagement Priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Global Principles reflect globally applicable elements of governance that contribute to long-term financial value; regional voting guidelines explain how Global Principles inform vote decisions in each market; Engagement Priorities cover the five themes BIS most frequently engages companies on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual policy review process
rubrics_metrics.description: BIS reviews its Benchmark Policies every year and updates them as necessary to reflect changes in market standards and regulations, feedback from clients and companies, and insights from research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review is rigorous yet flexible, enabling continuous improvement and pragmatic, case-by-case application of policies to vote for outcomes most aligned with clients' long-term financial interests. Changes may be language refinements or market-specific adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: An engagement is defined as a meeting with the boards and management of companies in which clients are invested; BIS counts only direct interaction as an engagement and does not count letters as engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagements are typically initiated by companies and are used to deepen understanding of business model, oversight of material risks/opportunities, and to inform voting decisions for clients who have authorized BIS to vote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement prioritization criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: BIS identifies and prioritizes companies for engagement based on several factors including identified or potential material financial risks, aggregate client exposure, corporate developments, changes in regulation, or other market developments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagement is determined to be helpful after assessing company disclosures; prioritization may consider where engagement can productively advance clients’ long-term financial interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement of engagement effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: BIS measures the effectiveness of engagements based on whether they helped lead to more informed voting decisions and/or deepened understanding of a company's business model and oversight of material risks and opportunities over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effectiveness assessments are used to inform stewardship reporting and case studies; outcomes may be reflected in subsequent voting or deeper understanding across multiple years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement Priority — Board quality and effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus stewardship efforts on the effectiveness of the board of directors because a strong board provides oversight and contributes to decisions that support long-term financial performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagement seeks to understand board composition, oversight practices, and how boards enable long-term value creation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement Priority — Strategy, purpose, and financial resilience
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage on long-term corporate strategy, purpose, and financial resilience to understand alignment of decision-making with company purpose and how strategy/capital allocation adapts as business dynamics change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversations probe how management and boards align strategy with purpose and sustain financial resilience through cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement Priority — Incentives aligned with financial value creation
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage where companies clearly disclose the connection between compensation policies and outcomes and the long-term financial interests of shareholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation favors transparent disclosures linking pay and long-term value creation; compensation structures are assessed for alignment with shareholder interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement Priority — Climate and natural capital
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage to understand companies’ approach to oversight of material climate-related risks and opportunities and management of material natural capital impacts and dependencies relative to their business model and sector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagement centers on materiality to the business model and sector-specific climate/natural-capital risks and how boards oversee them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement Priority — Company impacts on people
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage on how companies invest in relationships critical to strategic objectives, because such investments can support durable long-term financial performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topics include workforce practices, human capital management, and other people-related matters that materially affect performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting decision principles and inputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Vote decisions reflect BIS’ reasonable and independent judgment of what is in the long-term financial interests of clients and are informed by analysis of company disclosures, comparisons against industry peers, third-party research, and, where appropriate, engagement with companies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally support board/management recommendations where governance is sound and financial returns strong; analysts may exercise professional judgment when policies do not cover specific matters; may choose not to vote if voting costs outweigh benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision not to vote (cost-benefit consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: BIS may determine it is generally in clients' long-term financial interests not to vote proxies (or not to vote full allocation) if the costs (including opportunity costs like share-blocking) are expected to outweigh the benefits clients would derive by voting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voting incidence can be affected by market impediments such as share-blocking, sanctions, regulatory restrictions, and other logistical challenges; such instances are disclosed and explained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vote escalation process
rubrics_metrics.description: BIS has an escalation process enabling analysts and regional heads to raise high-profile and certain non-routine voting matters for further review by BIS’ regional heads and/or oversight committees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include shareholder activist situations, mergers, executive compensation proposals, and certain shareholder proposals. Escalation does not include filing shareholder proposals, proposing director candidates, or engaging in public campaigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of external proxy service vendor for routine items
rubrics_metrics.description: For routine agenda items with nothing contentious, BIS employs an external proxy service vendor to streamline voting by making recommendations according to BIS’ regional voting guidelines; non-routine/contentious items are referred to BIS analysts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vendor recommendations can be overridden prior to the vote deadline; both BIS and vendor monitor filings and disclosures for supplemental information that may change vote decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational voting controls and execution
rubrics_metrics.description: Dedicated operational specialists ensure votes are instructed successfully by identifying upcoming meetings, casting votes ahead of deadlines, reconciling holdings with ballots received, and identifying uninstructed ballots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controls and reconciliations are in place to ensure accurate vote execution across a large universe of companies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oversight of proxy research firms and service providers
rubrics_metrics.description: BIS oversees proxy research firms and service providers according to BlackRock’s global vendor oversight policies requiring thorough financial, operational, risk, and contract diligence and ongoing monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oversight includes weekly meetings with vendor client service teams, systematic monitoring of operations, escalation of issues, and annual due diligence meetings with senior leadership covering research quality, vote execution, conflicts management, continuity, and regulatory landscape.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence from proxy research firm recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: BIS makes voting decisions independently from any proxy research firm’s voting policy, using proxy research firms’ technology, data, and analysis only to support vote execution and operational processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clients with Voting Choice can opt for third-party policies; BIS' independent decisions may differ materially from proxy firms (example: BIS supported management in ~77% of cases where ISS recommended against in 2025).

rubrics_metrics.name: Management of conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: BlackRock maintains policies and procedures designed to prevent undue influence on BIS’ proxy voting activity stemming from relationships between investee companies (or proponents/dissidents) and BlackRock, its affiliates, funds, or employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BIS is a dedicated function separate from sales/business activities; where potential conflicts exist, BIS may outsource voting recommendations to an independent third-party voting service provider and publishes explanations and disclosures (example: Cisco case).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and assessment criteria for independent third-party voting service provider
rubrics_metrics.description: In selecting an independent third-party voting service provider BIS assesses characteristics including independence, ability to analyze proxy issues and make recommendations in the economic interest of clients in accordance with regional voting guidelines, reputation for reliability and integrity, and operational capacity to deliver recommendations timely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BIS may engage more than one provider to mitigate perceived conflicts, reviews recommendations annually post-season to ensure consistency with regional guidelines, reports findings to the BIS Global Oversight Committee, and meets the provider annually to discuss discrepancies and guideline changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality assurance: internal audit and external vote reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: BIS is audited periodically by BlackRock Internal Audit and contracts third-party specialists to review a sample of proxy votes and recommendations to ensure votes cast accurately reflect BIS’ regional voting guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal Audit uses a risk-based methodology; third-party reviews are reported to oversight committees as part of internal governance and assurance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting standards and client communication
rubrics_metrics.description: BIS informs clients about stewardship activities via a range of publications and client-specific engagement and voting reports; clients may request reporting on monthly, quarterly, or annual cadences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All BIS publications and client reports undergo rigorous internal review to ensure reporting is clear, balanced, and meets clients’ informational needs; BIS also provides quarterly updates and an expanded client-specific portfolio level engagement report with improved data visualization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and public disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: BIS publishes its benchmark policies, approach to various stewardship codes and directives, responses to policy consultations, and a Global Vote Disclosure tool that provides voting records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BIS explains when and why it takes different approaches relative to market-level stewardship codes (e.g., EU SRD II Engagement Policy, UK Stewardship Code) and provides access to consultation responses and ViewPoints to inform market dialogue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance structure and accountability for stewardship
rubrics_metrics.description: Governance comprises the Global Executive Committee setting firm strategic vision, BIS Global Co-Heads with primary oversight, the BIS Global Oversight Committee providing formal risk oversight of proxy voting, and BIS Leadership team promoting accountability and day-to-day guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The BIS Global Oversight Committee reviews votes and process issues in an oversight capacity, approves policy amendments annually, and confirms independent third-party provider appointments; the committee does not determine vote decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local presence and market-specific application
rubrics_metrics.description: BIS operates across nine offices with local teams to develop deep understanding of local market dynamics, regulation, and norms and applies global principles pragmatically across jurisdictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regional voting guidelines cover specific markets (ten markets noted) and local approach enables effective execution and adaptation to market-specific constraints such as share-blocking or local legal differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance metrics and disclosure of activity
rubrics_metrics.description: BIS reports quantitative stewardship metrics including numbers of engagements, companies engaged, proposals and meetings voted, and proportions of clients’ equity assets engaged; example disclosures include percentages of proposals by category and voting incidence (e.g., ~99% meetings voted in 2025).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metrics are sourced and dated (e.g., BlackRock, ISS, data from Jan 1–Dec 31, 2025) and are published in figures and the Global Vote Disclosure tool to provide transparency on activity and outcomes.
